## ✨ Highlights

- 🖥️ **Bare metal** - the same images now boot on real machines and on any disk: SATA, NVMe, USB, RAID/HBA controllers, server NICs, every CPU core, and the console on the screen as well as the serial port. The installer ISO goes on a USB stick.
- ⚡ **Every CPU** - the kernel was uniprocessor: every node, virtual machines included, used a single CPU. It now uses them all.
- 📦 **The Controller pushes updates** - a node that can't reach the internet can still be updated: the Controller downloads the bundle and pushes it to the node, with live progress.
- 🧩 **Extensions from the Controller** - change a node's extensions from its Update page, and only the apps a node has are listed, each with its own page and settings.
- 📈 **`prometheus-node-exporter`** - node-exporter is renamed and gets settings: listen address, port and collectors.

## 🖥️ Bare metal and hypervisors

- **Any disk**: the images no longer assume the first virtio disk (`/dev/vda`). They find their partitions by GPT label, so they boot as virtio, SATA/SAS/USB (`/dev/sda`) or NVMe (`/dev/nvme0n1`), and wait for a disk that shows up late.
- **Disks**: AHCI (SATA), NVMe, USB, virtio-blk and virtio-scsi (Proxmox's default controller), VMware pvscsi, Broadcom MegaRAID (Dell PERC), Broadcom/LSI SAS (mpt3sas), Microchip SmartPQI (HPE).
- **Network cards**: Intel e1000, e1000e, igb, igc, ixgbe, i40e; Realtek r8169; Broadcom tg3, bnxt; Mellanox ConnectX-4 and later (mlx5); VMware vmxnet3; virtio. Cards that need a firmware file (Intel ice, Broadcom bnx2x…) aren't supported.
- **CPUs**: SMP (up to 512 cores), x2APIC, NUMA, MSI-X.
- **Console on the screen**: the kernel's messages, the banner and the first-boot credentials appear on the screen (UEFI framebuffer) as well as on the serial port. On Proxmox, the noVNC console now shows them, so `vga: serial0` is no longer required.
- **The installer ISO** boots from a USB stick, or as a VM disk, and installs the machine's disk. It can't boot from a CD/DVD drive. See [provisioning a node, method 4](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/provisioning-a-node.md#method-4-the-installer-iso).
- **NoCloud** reads every disk type, CD-ROMs included - the kind of drive Proxmox's cloud-init uses (with Janus's own `user-data`, e.g. through `cicustom`).
- VMware's devices are tested under QEMU, not yet on a real ESXi host.

## 🖥️ Controller

- **The Controller pushes it**: a third way to deliver an update, next to "the node downloads it" and "upload files". The Controller downloads the bundle, streams it to the node (checking its sha256 on the way) and has the node install it, with live progress. The mode you pick is remembered.
- **Update › Change extensions…**: pick the extensions you want, and the Controller asks [janus.sw-servers.net](https://janus.sw-servers.net) for that image. If the image doesn't exist yet, its build starts and the page follows it; once it's ready, the form is filled in. The confirmation lists the extensions gained and lost, and the usual A/B update applies, with automatic revert.
- **Apps lists what the node has**: HAProxy, the Janus exporter, then the node's extensions and modules. Missing ones are no longer shown as "n/a"; **Add or remove apps…** opens the extensions panel.
- **Janus exporter** has its own page (settings moved from Metrics, plus a Prometheus scrape example). So do **Node exporter** (state and settings) and **QEMU guest agent** (state, what the hypervisor may do, and what to do while it waits for its channel).
- **Service logs** include the extensions' services.
- **The Controller's version** is shown on the main page and in each node's sidebar.

## 📈 prometheus-node-exporter

- `node-exporter` is renamed **`prometheus-node-exporter`** (the extension and its service).
- **Settings**, kept across reboots and upgrades: whether it runs, its listen address and port (9100 by default), and its collectors. You pick collectors from a list of those that work on a Janus node. Set them in the Controller (**Apps › Node exporter**), with `janusctl system node-exporter [-enable|-disable] [-address IP] [-port N] [-collectors a,b,c|default]`, or through `SystemService.NodeExporterConfigGet/Set`.
- The default `pressure` collector (CPU, memory and I/O pressure) now reports: the kernel gained PSI. `dmi` and `conntrack` work too.

## 🔒 Security

- SELinux: janusd can now read the processes of the `prometheus-node-exporter` and `qemu-guest-agent` extensions. Before, the process list and the Controller's metrics left them out, with a denial on every poll.
- Everything bare metal adds (the screen console, NUMA, the hardware's identity, disks partitioned by `Install`) runs under SELinux enforcing with zero denials.

## 🐛 Fixes

- The Controller's Update page could say "Unavailable" for 10 minutes on every node after a browser left the page at the wrong moment.
- When a node couldn't download its update (no route, connection refused), the error asked whether the bundle included a UKI. It now says the download failed, and suggests having the Controller push the bundle.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **HAProxy uses every CPU**: on a node with several CPUs, HAProxy now starts one thread per CPU unless your configuration sets `nbthread`.
- **Nodes with `node-exporter`**: the update to this release is offered as a rename.
  - **Controller**: the Update page shows "node-exporter is now called prometheus-node-exporter". **Use this update** fills everything in, including the schematic change.
  - **janusctl**: pass `-allow-schematic-change`.
  - Prometheus still scrapes `:9100`. The service's logs are now under `prometheus-node-exporter`.
- **Update the Controller** (`swenske/janus-controller:v2026.10.01-3` or `:latest`) to get the push mode, the extensions panel and node_exporter's settings. node_exporter's settings need the node on this release; on older nodes, the page says so.
